sources.entry: Rapid Reader - Open-source RSVP speed reader for EPUB, PDF, and web articles with a full-text view. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Zer0codestuff/Rapid-Reader) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Rapid Reader is a free, open-source native macOS app that combines RSVP (rapid serial visual presentation) speed reading with a normal full-text reader for EPUB, PDF, and web articles.
summary.what_it_does: Imports EPUB, PDF, DOCX, RTF, HTML, Markdown, plain text, pasted text, and web articles into a local library that tracks reading progress, favorites, notes, preferences, sections, and EPUB cover art. In RSVP mode it shows words one at a time with pivot-letter highlighting, context preview, punctuation pauses, and adjustable chunk size. Full-text mode lets you browse the original text and click a word to resume from that position. The app also offers in-document search, light/dark/sepia themes, and a Statistics view for reading time and speed. A browser version is also mentioned, with a separate library stored in the browser. Data is stored locally in ~/Library/Application Support/Rapid Reader.
use_cases: speed read books and long articles on a Mac
read EPUB or PDF files one word at a time
resume reading from a specific word in a document
read web articles without an account
track reading progress and speed locally
read ebooks in a browser without installing an app
how_to_run: Download RapidReader-.dmg from the GitHub Releases page
Open the DMG and drag Rapid Reader.app into Applications
Launch Rapid Reader (if blocked, allow it in System Settings -> Privacy & Security)
Build from source: ./script/build_and_run.sh (or --build-only to build without launching)
notable: Full-text and RSVP modes linked by click-to-resume position
Local-only library with no account or cloud sync required
Universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs
Comparison table with Outread and Spreeder in the README
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or newer and Xcode command line tools with a Swift 6 toolchain to build from source
Release builds are ad-hoc signed unless notarized, so macOS may block the first launch
Auto-updates via Sparkle are enabled only in builds made with SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY
